paper_metadata.title: Quantum Risk Analysis of Financial Derivatives

summary: This paper develops two gate-based quantum algorithms for derivative-portfolio risk estimation: a QAE-based VaR method and a QSP-based VaR/CVaR method. In numerical simulations, QSP required about 10x fewer oracle calls than QAE for the same VaR error, and the authors estimate that for N = 50,000 scenarios the logical clock rate required for quantum advantage could be reduced by up to about 30x relative to single-derivative pricing, contingent on efficient scenario preparation.

experiments.description: Quantum algorithm for estimating Value at Risk (VaR) of derivative portfolios using Quantum Amplitude Estimation (QAE) with scenario superposition and coherent inner pricing.

algorithm.variant: QAE-based VaR estimation for derivative portfolios
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Bisection search over VaR candidate µ until estimated P[V ≤ µ] reaches 1−α within target amplitude-estimation accuracy
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Start bisection with µ_l=0 and µ_h=1

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Scenario register |s⟩ encodes market-state tweaks; derivative value is encoded into an amplitude via oracle A, then QAE coherently estimates the portfolio value under each scenario
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate VaR_α[V] = V0 − µ_α where µ_α is the smallest threshold such that P[V ≤ µ_α] ≥ 1−α
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Binary comparator C_µ marks whether encoded value is below threshold; bisection search used to locate VaR threshold

problem_instance.description: Derivative portfolio VaR estimation across multiple market scenarios

dataset_specification.description: Scenarios are modeled either by Monte Carlo or historical sampling; no specific market dataset is named

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Scenario values normalized to [0,1] for the analysis; portfolio values under scenarios are priced and compared to threshold µ
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Numerical simulation of QAE-based VaR algorithm; paper compares against classical VaR estimates and reports resource scaling, but does not specify a fixed number of independent runs for this experiment

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Scenario generation and classical pricing of each scenario for baseline comparisons
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Bisection search and percentile selection for VaR baseline

results.value: approximately linear decrease in VaR error with oracle calls on a log-log scale (slope ≈ -0.9)

classical_baselines.value: classical VaR estimate from same sampled scenarios; no explicit numeric error reported

speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical nested Monte Carlo VaR estimation
speedup_claims.conditions: when comparing asymptotic scaling in inner pricing accuracy
speedup_claims.caveats: The improvement is in the pricing subroutine and overall VaR estimation under the paper’s assumptions; scenario loading may dominate in practice.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O((C(ϵ_S)+ϵ_p^{-1})ϵ_A^{-1}) for estimating P[X≤µ]; with sampled scenarios and efficient loading, ˜O(ϵ_p^{-1}ϵ_A^{-1})
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(ϵ_S^{-2}ϵ_p^{-2}) for nested Monte Carlo VaR estimation
complexity_analysis.total_operations_quantum: QAE VaR uses 2^m+1 oracle calls to A/A† for the inner value-encoding step, plus outer QAE calls; exact total depends on bisection rounds and target accuracies

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not reported as a concrete problem size; analysis is asymptotic and symbolic.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: QAE VaR scales as O((C(ε_S)+ε_p^-1)ε_A^-1); with sampled scenarios and efficient loading, ~O(ε_p^-1 ε_A^-1).
limiting_factors: Scenario-state preparation cost is left as an open variable
Nested amplitude estimation and bisection add substantial overhead

notes: No specific hardware or qubit count is reported for the QAE experiment; the paper is theoretical/numerical and discusses resource scaling rather than a concrete device run.

num_qubits and circuit_depth are inferred as not specified because the paper gives symbolic register sizes (e.g., m qubits for value encoding) but no instantiated experiment-wide qubit count or depth for a concrete benchmark.
The paper presents a theoretical QAE-based VaR algorithm and complexity analysis, but no experimental hardware result.
The authors discuss possible quantum advantage only conditionally, not as a demonstrated benchmark win.

experiments.description: Quantum algorithm for estimating Value at Risk (VaR) of derivative portfolios using Quantum Signal Processing (QSP) to apply a threshold function to block-encoded portfolio values, followed by QAE readout.

algorithm.variant: QSP-based VaR estimation with polynomial threshold approximation
algorithm.optimizer: optimization-based minimax polynomial fitting for Chebyshev coefficients
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Bisection search over µ until estimated P[|G⟩] reaches 1−α within target amplitude-estimation accuracy
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Bisection starts with µ_l=0 and µ_h=1; polynomial coefficients are obtained by optimization over Chebyshev basis

optimizer_settings.objective: minimax approximation error over discretized grid

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Derivative price is block-encoded via oracle A; QSP applies a polynomial approximation to the threshold function θ_µ(x) on the singular values √V(s)
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate VaR_α[V] = V0 − µ_α where µ_α is the smallest threshold such that P[V ≤ µ_α] ≥ 1−α
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Threshold function approximation via QSP; bisection search and QAE used to estimate the marked-state probability

problem_instance.description: Derivative portfolio VaR estimation across multiple market scenarios using QSP

dataset_specification.description: Scenario prices in simulations are drawn from a normal distribution with mean 0.5 and standard deviation 0.09; 5k scenarios per sample in the resource comparison study

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Scenario prices normalized to [0,1]; polynomial threshold approximations generated for µ values during bisection
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Numerical simulation over 100 independent samples for each data point in the QSP-vs-QAE comparison; for the advantage study, 200 repetitions are used to estimate error distributions

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Scenario generation from a normal distribution and classical VaR computation by sorting
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Bisection search and percentile selection for VaR baseline

speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical nested Monte Carlo VaR estimation
speedup_claims.conditions: when comparing asymptotic scaling and assuming efficient scenario loading
speedup_claims.caveats: QSP reduces constant factors versus QAE and avoids intermediate binary digitization, but still requires QAE readout and polynomial approximation error.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O((C(ϵ_S)+ϵ_θ^{-1})ϵ_A^{-1}); with sampled scenarios and efficient loading, ˜O(ϵ_θ^{-1}ϵ_A^{-1})
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(ϵ_S^{-2}ϵ_p^{-2}) for nested Monte Carlo VaR estimation
complexity_analysis.total_operations_quantum: QSP VaR uses d−1 invocations of A per threshold evaluation, plus QAE oracle calls; end-to-end T-depth is given symbolically in the paper as T_QSP = 2.8k/ϵ_A * log(2/α_k * log2(π/(4ϵ_A))) * (T_S + dT_A + 3d log2(1/ϵ_R))

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not reported as a concrete crossover; the paper gives symbolic T-depth and oracle-call formulas only.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: QSP VaR uses d-1 invocations of A per threshold evaluation; end-to-end T-depth is given by T_QSP = 2.8k/ε_A * log(2/α_k * log2(π/(4ε_A))) * (T_S + dT_A + 3d log2(1/ε_R)).
limiting_factors: Quadratic speedup relative to classical sampling in the reported regime
Polynomial approximation degree and QAE accuracy must both be large for useful precision

notes: The paper reports symbolic circuit structure and an end-to-end T-depth formula, but no concrete qubit count for a specific hardware run.
circuit_depth is reported symbolically via the T-depth expression and the number of QSP/QAE oracle invocations; no transpiled depth is given.
The paper reports a numerical resource comparison showing QSP uses about 10x fewer oracle calls than QAE for the same VaR error.
This is not a practical end-to-end advantage demonstration on hardware.

experiments.description: Quantum advantage benchmark for QSP-based VaR estimation versus classical Monte Carlo VaR estimation for an autocallable derivative product, estimating the logical QPU clock rate required for parity/advantage as a function of scenario-preparation T-depth.

algorithm.convergence_criteria: Search over polynomial degree d and amplitude-estimation accuracy ϵ_A to match classical VaR error; then compute required logical clock rate
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Scenario prices sampled from a normal distribution; µ averaged over [0.45, 0.48, 0.5, 0.52, 0.55] for the quantum benchmark

optimizer_settings.objective: match quantum VaR error to classical VaR error while minimizing T-depth / required logical clock rate

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Autocallable derivative pricing oracle A is used inside the QSP VaR circuit; scenario superposition is loaded and thresholded via polynomial approximation
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate the minimum logical QPU clock rate needed for QSP VaR to match classical VaR runtime at equal error
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Bisection search over VaR threshold; QAE used to estimate marked-state probability

problem_instance.description: Autocallable derivative product benchmark from prior derivative-pricing work, used here for VaR advantage analysis

dataset_specification.description: Scenario prices drawn from N(µ, σ^2) with σ=0.09; benchmark averaged over µ ∈ [0.45, 0.48, 0.5, 0.52, 0.55]

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Classical benchmark prices N scenarios in one second each; quantum benchmark uses the same sampled scenario prices and searches for d, ϵ_A that match classical error
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 200 repetitions for each N; compare 68th-percentile quantum error to classical one-standard-deviation error; compute required logical clock rate as T_QSP / N

implementation_details.classical_solver: classical Monte Carlo VaR with one-second-per-scenario pricing assumption
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Generate scenario prices from a normal distribution and compute classical VaR by sorting
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compare quantum and classical VaR errors; derive logical clock rate threshold for advantage

results.value: up to ~30x reduction in required logical clock rate

classical_baselines.value: 45 MHz reference for single-derivative pricing; classical VaR runtime assumed N seconds for N scenarios

speedup_claims.factor: up to ~30x reduction in required logical clock rate
speedup_claims.baseline_method: single-derivative pricing threshold from Ref. [19] / classical Monte Carlo VaR benchmark
speedup_claims.conditions: for N = 50,000 and scenario superposition preparation T-depth TS ≲ 3×10^5; advantage possible for TS ≲ 8×10^7
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a resource-estimation benchmark, not a hardware demonstration; advantage depends strongly on scenario-preparation cost and assumes fault-tolerant logical execution.

complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Classical end-to-end VaR runtime assumed to scale linearly with the number of scenarios N (N seconds for N scenarios under the paper’s benchmark assumption)
complexity_analysis.total_operations_quantum: For the benchmark, the paper reports that for N=50k the QSP method can reduce the logical clock rate required for advantage by up to ~30x relative to single-derivative pricing, depending on scenario-preparation cost
complexity_analysis.crossover_n: Advantage possible for N=50k if scenario superposition can be prepared with T-depth TS ≲ 8×10^7; ~30x reduction in required logical clock rate if TS ≲ 3×10^5

notes: This is a resource-estimation/advantage study, not a hardware execution experiment.
The paper reports T-depth formulas and threshold values for scenario-preparation T-depth, but not a concrete qubit count for the benchmark circuit.
The reported advantage is conditional and benchmark-specific; the paper does not claim an unconditional asymptotic speedup over the best classical VaR methods.

algorithm.convergence_criteria: Average VaR error versus number of oracle calls; 100 independent samples per data point

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Compares QAE and QSP implementations for VaR estimation using the same scenario-price model and classical baseline
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate VaR error as a function of oracle calls and amplitude-estimation accuracy

problem_instance.description: Synthetic scenario-price benchmark for VaR estimation
